title: G-A-L
hook: geulah, go'el: redeem, as a relative redeems family land

segments.voice: Yesterday, M-L-Ch: melech and malchut, a king asked for and a kingdom accepted. Your line was kingship. What did you catch ruling your day, and did you crown it? Today, a word for what a family does when something is lost. Day one thousand three hundred seventy-eight.

Midnight, on a threshing floor. The barley harvest is in, and a landowner named Boaz has fallen asleep beside the grain heap. He wakes with a start: someone is lying at his feet. "Who art thou?" A widow, Ruth, the foreigner who has been gleaning in his field. She doesn't ask for money. She asks him to spread his cloak over her, and gives her reason in a single phrase. In the King James: "for thou art a near kinsman." That phrase, near kinsman, is one Hebrew word: go'el. Today's root.
screen: `MIDNIGHT ON THE THRESHING FLOOR.` → `WHO ART THOU?` → `FOR THOU ART A NEAR KINSMAN.`

segments.voice: G-A-L. Gimel, alef, lamed. Go'el, the one who redeems. Geulah, redemption. Turn it four ways. First, the law behind the word. In Leviticus, if a man falls into poverty and sells part of his land, in the King James: "if any of his kin come to redeem it, then shall he redeem that which his brother sold." To redeem is to buy back. The go'el is the relative who steps in so the family doesn't lose its ground. Second, the gate. The morning after the threshing floor, Boaz sits at the town gate, because there's a relative closer than he is, with the first right to redeem a field that belonged to Naomi's late husband. That man is ready to buy the field, until he learns Ruth comes with it. Then he backs away: "I cannot redeem it for myself." Boaz steps in, and the land and the family stay together. Third, God as go'el. Back in Egypt, before the plagues, God says to the enslaved people: "I will redeem you with a stretched out arm." The same word. God is cast as the near relative who comes to buy the family back. Fourth, the prayer. In the weekday Amidah, one blessing calls God go'el Yisrael, the redeemer of Israel, and geulah, redemption, is something Jews still pray toward. So redemption in this root isn't vague. It looks like a relative walking to the gate and paying what it costs to bring someone home.
screen: `THE GO'EL BUYS BACK THE LAND.` · `A CLOSER KINSMAN SAYS NO.` · `I WILL REDEEM YOU.` · `GO'EL YISRAEL, IN THE AMIDAH.` · then, large: `גּוֹאֵל · גְּאֻלָּה`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: redeem one situation. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind something that slipped away from where it should be. A friendship gone quiet after a sharp word. A promise half kept. A neighbor whose trash can blew over and never got picked up. Your own garden, gone to weeds. Something that could still be bought back. Ask what it would cost: a phone call, an apology, an hour, a bit of pride. Then decide on the one step you'll take, the way Boaz walked to the gate. If you pray, you can ask for help with it. The bell holds the time.
screen: `WHAT WOULD IT COST TO BUY BACK?`

segments.voice: G-A-L. Gimel, alef, lamed: go'el, the near relative who buys back what was lost, and geulah, redemption. Today's word.
Your line: redeem. Today, take that one step: make the call, pay the cost, walk to the gate. Day one thousand three hundred seventy-eight.

howItsDone: Jews read the book of Ruth on Shavuot, and the weekday Amidah includes a blessing to God as go'el Yisrael, the redeemer of Israel; geulah, redemption, is a hope that runs through Jewish prayer.

notes: Quotations from the KJV; confirm the Judaism path accepts KJV here.
Ruth 3:9 'near kinsman' renders go'el; confirm. 'Who art thou?' is also KJV Ruth 3:9 (quoted in the hook, same verse).
The threshing floor is placed 'outside Bethlehem' from the book's setting; the text does not say exactly where. Soften if needed.
Ruth 4: the closer relative first agrees to redeem the field and declines when told he must also take Ruth; the script compresses this. Confirm framing.
'Before the plagues' for Exodus 6:6 is narrative order; confirm.
Reading of Ruth on Shavuot in howItsDone is widespread custom; confirm.

Editor: cut 'outside Bethlehem' (the text does not place the threshing floor); 'daily Amidah' corrected to 'weekday Amidah', since the Shabbat Amidah lacks the go'el Yisrael blessing. Ruth also appeared on day 1367 (the road from Moab); this day uses a different scene.
